---
title: "Learn Proteomics"
---

## Proteomics basics

Mass spectrometry measures peptide signals that can be matched to protein sequences. A typical analysis moves from **raw instrument files** to **identified peptides**, then **protein groups**, quantified values, and biological interpretation.

## DDA versus DIA

| Approach | Basic idea | Typical use |
|---|---|---|
| DDA | Selects individual precursor ions for fragmentation. | Discovery experiments and spectral-library generation. |
| DIA | Fragments all ions within sequential mass windows. | Consistent, deep quantitative proteomics. |

## Concepts to know

- **FASTA:** protein-sequence database used for peptide identification.
- **Spectral library:** reference collection of observed peptide spectra.
- **FDR:** estimated false discovery rate; a measure used to control confidence.
- **QC:** quality-control checks that identify problems before interpretation.
- **Protein inference:** grouping peptide evidence into protein-level results.

## Software concepts

**Spectronaut** supports DIA processing with a graphical workflow and report exports. **DIA-NN** is a fast command-line tool that supports library-free DIA analysis. Both require documented settings, an approved FASTA database, and quality-control review.
